page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c4g1.xlarge is a KVM-hypervised instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, with a 40 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.5 GB per core. For acceleration, it includes a single NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Storage is provided via a local 472 GB SSD, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear divergence between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The Intel Xeon CPU exhibits weak to poor performance across standard compute benchmarks, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core scores placing in the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 10%. Similarly, database operations and static web serving throughput register in the bottom 25%. However, the integrated NVIDIA P100 GPU delivers strong results in specific workloads, achieving top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing and text generation for medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a specialized hardware profile where value is concentrated in the bundled GPU and local SSD storage rather than raw CPU compute or memory speed. Users face a tradeoff: while the CPU and memory subsystem underperform relative to modern general-purpose instances, the presence of dedicated Pascal-generation GPU acceleration makes it a viable option for legacy machine learning workloads.

The ecs.gn5-c4g1.xlarge is suited for workloads that can offload processing to the GPU, such as small to medium-scale LLM inference, legacy deep learning model execution, and GPU-accelerated data processing. It is less suitable for CPU-heavy tasks, high-throughput database operations, or memory-intensive applications that do not leverage the GPU.
